text: fibers. The cutting trials were established for a range of fiber types. For all variants the fiber length had close to zero SD and hence perfect cuts. Glass fiber cuts were perfect in all respects – exact cut length and full filamentization. For TCF, the cut fibers were influenced by the sizing / binding and hence did not fully filamentize.. The filamentizing varied for different sizing and fiber lengths. For 72 e.g. the 1” fibers dispersed more than the ½” fiber length. A full study was conducted to provide learning for the epoxy and urethane sizing of the TCF Kaltex and Montefibre fibers. Using air blast was found to be an effective way to obtain better filamentization. While this greatly helped, air blast was not fully optimized within this project – but provided sufficient indication of its effectiveness. The study also demonstrated the utility of the line to cut and produce basalt fiber SMC. Basalt from Mafic was evaluated in different sizings: some fiber types were perfectly cut while some had resistance to cut (more tacky sizing). Full characterization of fiber length and width were conducted for the basalt fiber runs. A limited amount of basalt-vinyl ester SMC was also produced. The weight fraction consistency was established in all trials. Innovations in hybrid SMC were established. Initial trials were conducted on the properties from recycled carbon fiber (rCF) mats in epoxy resin. The rCF mats were effectively integrated in the glass SMC (20 wt%) production to provide glass-rCF hybrid SMC. Property bounds were established for the hybrid SMC in terms of flexural properties. Additional studies will be conducted to include a range of weight fractions. The hybrid SMC concept was also extended to include TCF substrate with glass-SMC in an overmolding configuration. This provided impressive strength and modulus gains, even by adding a single layer of TCF substrate to SMC. Various concepts were investigated in terms of the hybrid SMC. The rCF entangled fibers were subjected to resonant acoustic mixing, followed by carding and mat preparation. The lower-upper bound properties from the carded rCF were established. Concepts for adding the RAM-carder in- line to the SMC were also discussed. A detailed study included in Appendix A was conducted to establish tensile, flexural, interlaminar shear and Izod impact properties for glass-SMC and TCF-SMC. Properties are dependent on fiber weight fraction and only 30 wt% were studied in this study. Overall, the Covid19 situation constrained the team from accessing the SMC line for over 18 months. Despite this challenge major advancements were made. The cutting of glass fiber and TCF (different precursor based) was illustrated via videos.
